regions.name: Kugti
features: Kugti Wildlife Sanctuary is located in the Chambal district of Himachal Pradesh.
It was established in 1962, spanning an area of about 379 sq km.
Since it is situated at a high-altitude terrain, it is home to the endangered Himalayan Tahr.

regions.name: Abohar
features: Abohar Wildlife Sanctuary is located in the Fazilka district in Punjab.
It is unique because it is an open sanctuary comprising farmlands of 13 Bishnoi villages.
It is famous for the conservation of the blackbuck ( Indian antelope) and other wildlife found here are the blue bull (nilgai), hare, porcupine, and various bird species.

regions.name: Bhimbandh
features: Bhimbandh Wildlife Sanctuary is located in Bihar and has several hot water springs of which Bhimbandh is the most famous.
Its rich biodiversity includes  tigers, leopards, wild boar, nilgai, and several bird species
It covers an area of 681.99 sq km.

regions.name: Radhanagari
features: Radhanagari Wildlife Sanctuary is located in the state of Maharashtra and occupies an area of 351.16 sq km.
It is one of the few remaining habitats for the Indian Bison (Gaur), which is an endangered animal.

regions.name: Mount Abu
features: Mount Abu Wildlife Sanctuary is located in Rajasthan and covers an area of 288 sq km.
It was established in 1980.
It is home to a variety of animals, including the Indian Leopard, sloth bear, Sambar deer, wild boar and chinkara.
Mount Abu is the only place in Rajasthan where one can see a variety of orchids.

regions.name: Hazaribagh
features: Hazaribagh Wildlife Sanctuary is located in Jharkhand and is about 186 sq km.
It was accorded the status of a wildlife sanctuary in 1954.
The Hazaribagh Wildlife Sanctuary has a rich biodiversity. The habitat is also shared by chital, wild boars, black bears, jackals, porcupines, hyenas, pangolins, hares, etc.

regions.name: Rupi Bhaba
features: Rupi Bhaba is located in the state of Himachal Pradesh.
The sanctuary is named after Rupi and Bhawa valleys and spans about 503 square kilometres.
The Hazaribagh Wildlife Sanctuary has a rich biodiversity. The habitat is also shared by chital, wild boars, black bears, jackals, porcupines, hyenas, pangolins, hares, etc.

regions.name: Gandhi sagar
features: Gandhi Sagar Wildlife Sanctuary is located in the state of Madhya Pradesh.
It is located along the banks of the River Chambal and has dense forests and grasslands.
It is a crucial habitat for many animals and bird species.

regions.name: Yaval
features: The Yawal Wildlife Sanctuary is located inb the state of Maharashtra.
It is spread over an area of 178 square kilometres.
The sanctuary has many different mammals and the flying squirrel is a special attraction here.

regions.name: Melghat
features: Melghat Tiger Reserve is located in the state of Maharashtra.
It was established as a wildlife sanctuary in 1967 and later declared a Tiger Reserve in 1974.
It is one of the biggest tiger reserves in terms of area in India.

regions.name: Eturnagaram
features: Eturnagaram Wildlife Sanctuary is located in the state of Telangana.
It encompasses an area of 806 square kilometres and has diverse flora and fauna.

regions.name: Pakhal
features: Pakhal Wildlife Sanctuary is located in the state of Telangana.
It got its name from the beautiful Pakhal lake around which this sanctuary is located.
It has mixed deciduous forests and covers an area of 839 square kilometres.

regions.name: Pocharam
features: Pocharam Wildlife Sanctuary is located in the state of Telangana.
The sanctuary encompasses an area of 130 square kilometres.
The sanctuary has diverse fauna such as Wild Dog, Leopard, Wolf, Jackal, Forest Cat, Sloth Bear, Sambar, Nilgai, Chinkara, Chital, and four-horned Antelope.

regions.name: Nagarjuna Sagar
features: Nagarjuna Sagar Wildlife Sanctuary is now Nagarajunasagar Srisailam Tiger Reserve (NSTR) located in the state of Andhra Pradesh.
It was granted the status of a Tiger Reserve in 1983.
It is India’s largest Tiger Reserve.

regions.name: Bhagwan Mahavir
features: Bhagwan Mahavir Wildlife Sanctuary is located in the state of Goa.
It encompasses an area of 240 square kilometres.
It is the largest wildlife preserve within the state of Goa.

regions.name: Mudumalai
features: Mudumalai Tiger Reserve is located in the state of Tamil Nadu.
It is spread over 688.59 square kilometres.
It is situated at the tri-junction of three states: Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Kerala.

regions.name: Jaldapara
features: Jaldapara National Park is located in the state of West Bengal.
Jaldapara was declared as a wildlife sanctuary in 1941 for the protection of the Indian One-Horned Rhino, and in 2012, it was declared as a National Park.
It covers an area of 216 square kilometres.
It has herds of Bison, Hispid hare, Hog deer, Sambar, and Asian elephants amongst other animals.

regions.name: Kaimur
features: The Kaimur Wildlife Sanctuary is located in the state of Bihar.
It spans an area of 1500 square kilometres.
This sanctuary is a plateau with lush forests.

regions.name: Dalma
features: Dalma Wildlife Sanctuary is located in the state of Jharkhand.
It was inaugurated in 1975 and has a sizable population of Indian elephants.

regions.name: Intanki
features: The Intanki National park is located in the state of Nagaland.
It encompasses an area of 202.02 square kilometres.
It was declared as a National park in the year 1993.
It was also declared as an elephant reserve by the government in 2005.

regions.name: Bhitarkanika
features: Bhitarkanika Wildlife Sanctuary is located in the state of Odisha.
It is famous for its Tidal mangroves.
It covers an area of approximately 672 square kilometres.
The saltwater crocodile is a permanent resident here and this sanctuary is a habitat for migratory birds.
